questions.prompt: A model has 2% training error and 25% validation error. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Overfitting (high variance): the model memorizes the training set
Irreducible noise that no model could ever remove
The validation set is mislabeled, while training itself is fine
Underfitting (high bias): the model is too simple for the data
questions.explanation: A large gap with low training error indicates high variance. Remedies: more data, regularization, a simpler model.

questions.prompt: Observations have noise standard deviation 0.4. A model achieves test MSE 0.25. How much of the test MSE is reducible (above the irreducible noise floor)? Give a number with 2 decimals.
questions.explanation: Irreducible error is sigma^2 = 0.16; reducible = 0.25 - 0.16 = 0.09 (bias^2 + variance).

questions.prompt: Both training and validation error plateau at 0.28 as the training set grows, while the target is 0.10. What should you do?
options: Add stronger regularization to reduce the remaining variance
Collect ten times more data, because the validation gap will close
Increase model capacity or improve features; more data will not help
Shuffle the test set again so the plateau moves lower
questions.explanation: Converging high errors are the signature of high bias.

questions.prompt: At one input the true value is 1.0. Models fitted on four training sets predict 0.9, 1.3, 1.1, 1.1. What is the bias squared of the average model? Give a number with 3 decimals.
questions.explanation: The mean prediction is 1.1; bias = 0.1 so bias^2 = 0.010.

questions.prompt: You pick the 10 best features from 1000 using all labels, then run 5-fold CV on those 10 features. The labels are random. What does CV report?
options: Accuracy far above chance, because the selection used the validation labels
About 50%, because with random labels no feature can help
Exactly 50%, because cross-validation always balances random labels
An error, because scikit-learn forbids selecting features before CV
questions.explanation: Selection must be repeated inside each training fold, otherwise validation information leaks.

questions.prompt: 103 samples are split into 5 folds with sizes as equal as possible. How many samples are in the smallest training set used by the five fits? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: Folds: 21,21,21,20,20. Training sizes are 103-21 = 82 or 103-20 = 83; the smallest is 82.

questions.prompt: A grasp-success classifier scores 98% on a random split of robot trials but 71% when tested on a new robot. Give two possible causes and explain how you would distinguish them and change the evaluation protocol.
rubric: Names distribution shift (hardware, lighting, gripper) and/or leakage from near-duplicate trials in the random split.
Distinguishes them: domain classifier AUC, group-wise split by robot/session, compare train/val on the old robot.
Proposes group splits (by robot, site, date), a final untouched test set, and reporting with confidence intervals.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
